title: SQL Snippets & Database Tips
subtitle: Handy database queries and techniques for managing your data like a pro - think of these as your database recipe cards! 🗃️

intro.title: 📖 About This Guide
paragraphs: Database work can seem intimidating, but with the right snippets in your toolkit, you'll be querying data like a seasoned professional! This collection includes practical SQL examples for common tasks - from date formatting to finding duplicates.

Each snippet is like a tried-and-true recipe - tested, reliable, and ready to use in your own projects. Whether you're a beginner learning the basics or an experienced developer looking for a quick reference, these examples will serve you well.

items.title: ISO 8601 Date Conversion
items.body: Convert any date to the standard ISO format with UTC timezone marker. Perfect for APIs and data exchange!

callout.text: This converts your local time to UTC and adds the Z at the end.

items.title: Date Range Queries
items.body: Find records within a specific date range the safe way that handles time zones properly.

code.content:
SELECT *
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate >= '2015-01-01'
  AND OrderDate <  '2015-02-01';

callout.text: Using >= and < instead of BETWEEN avoids timezone confusion at midnight.

items.title: PIVOT - Turn Rows into Columns
items.body: Transform your data from long format to wide format. Great for creating summary reports!

code.content:
DECLARE @lyr VARCHAR(4) = YEAR(DATEADD(yyyy, -1, GETDATE()));

SELECT *
FROM (
        SELECT 
            basecard,
            YEAR(docdate) AS [Year],
            CONVERT(VARCHAR(3), DATEADD(M, MONTH(docdate), -1), 107) AS MONTHS,
            linetotal
        FROM mytbl
        WHERE YEAR(docdate) >= @lyr
    ) AS P
PIVOT
(
    SUM(linetotal)
    FOR MONTHS IN (Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, [Dec])
) AS PVT
ORDER BY basecard, [Year];

callout.text: This turns month rows into columns for easy year-over-year summaries.

items.title: Conditional Aggregation
items.body: Calculate different totals in one query using CASE statements.

code.content:
SELECT 
    CustomerID,
    SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(OrderDate) = 2015 THEN Total END) AS Total2015,
    SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(OrderDate) = 2014 THEN Total END) AS Total2014
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;

items.title: Row Numbers
items.body: Add sequential numbers to your results - perfect for pagination or ranking.

code.content:
SELECT *, 
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT 0)) AS rn
FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT 
            *
        FROM YourTable
     ) AS T
ORDER BY rn;

items.title: LEAD and LAG - Compare with Previous or Next
items.body: Look at the row before or after the current one. Great for tracking changes over time.

code.content:
SELECT
    EmployeeID,
    PayDate,
    Salary,
    LAG(Salary, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY EmployeeID ORDER BY PayDate) AS PrevSalary,
    LEAD(Salary, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY EmployeeID ORDER BY PayDate) AS NextSalary
FROM Payroll;

callout.text: Perfect for salary changes, stock prices, or any time-based comparisons.

items.title: Find Duplicate Records
items.body: Spot those pesky duplicates before they cause problems in your reports.

code.content:
SELECT ColumnA, COUNT(*) AS Cnt
FROM MyTable
GROUP BY ColumnA
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

items.title: Remove Duplicates (Keep One)
items.body: Clean up duplicates while keeping one good copy.

code.content:
WITH dupes AS (
    SELECT 
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ColumnA ORDER BY (SELECT 0)) AS rn
    FROM MyTable
)
DELETE FROM dupes WHERE rn > 1;

callout.text: Always backup your data before running DELETE statements.

items.title: Find Gaps in Sequential Numbers
items.body: Identify missing numbers in a sequence - useful for invoice numbers, order IDs, and more.

code.content:
SELECT t1.ID + 1 AS MissingStart
FROM Numbers t1
LEFT JOIN Numbers t2 ON t2.ID = t1.ID + 1
WHERE t2.ID IS NULL;

items.title: CROSS APPLY - Correlated Subqueries Made Easy
items.body: Get related data for each row efficiently, like looking up the last order for each customer.

code.content:
SELECT 
    c.CustomerID,
    x.LastOrderDate
FROM Customers c
CROSS APPLY (
    SELECT MAX(OrderDate) AS LastOrderDate
    FROM Orders o
    WHERE o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
) AS x;

items.title: String Aggregation
items.body: Combine multiple rows into a comma-separated list - the old-school way that still works everywhere.

code.content:
SELECT 
    Department,
    STUFF((
        SELECT ', ' + EmployeeName
        FROM Employees e2
        WHERE e2.Department = e1.Department
        FOR XML PATH(''), TYPE
    ).value('.', 'VARCHAR(MAX)'), 1, 2, '') AS EmployeeList
FROM Employees e1
GROUP BY Department;

callout.text: In SQL Server 2017+, you can use STRING_AGG() instead.

items.title: Update with JOIN
items.body: Update records based on data from another table. Very powerful for data maintenance.

code.content:
UPDATE t
SET t.Status = 'Inactive'
FROM Users t
JOIN UserLogin u ON u.UserID = t.UserID
WHERE u.LastLogin < '2015-01-01';

callout.text: Always test UPDATE statements with SELECT before running them.

items.title: Always Test First
items.body: Before running UPDATE or DELETE statements, test them as SELECT queries first.

items.title: Use Descriptive Names
items.body: Name your columns and aliases clearly. Future you and your coworkers will thank you.

items.title: Index Your Joins
items.body: Make sure the columns you're joining on have indexes so the database can work efficiently.

items.title: Be Specific
items.body: Use specific date ranges and WHERE clauses. Don't pull more data than you need.

footer.heading: SQL Mastery Achieved!
footer.text: Remember: Your data is only as good as your queries.
